document.abstract: Zone plate techniques are not new; the detailed theory is well documented in technical literature dating back several years. But the concepts have not yet seen widespread application or understanding, particularly in the United States. A conceptual description of zone plate signal generation is presented, with comparisons between simple zone plate patterns and more common test signals. The more complex patterns, with their ability to exercise a system in horizontal, vertical, and temporal (motion) dimensions, are discussed in light of the sophisticated processing required for practical recording and/or transmission of the greater information content of enhanced or High Definition video.

authors.bio: During his 29 years with Tektronix, John Horn has been design engineer, project leader, and group manager responsible for circuit design and product development of various television waveform monitors, vectorscopes, and color picture displays. He presently is manager of the Technology Development Group in Tektronix' Television Division in Beaverton, Oregon. Horn has written numerous articles on video signal measurement, evaluation, and display, and holds several patents on innovations in these areas.
